items.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023
items.q: Gary Bartz is going to do some and Roy Ayers is going to do some.

ctx.x: Well thanks for sharing that. I’d like to — before we’re done here I want to just ask you about the last few years. It’s been interesting because some of your music from the 70s has been revisited and now they’re calling it classic, and at the same time you got hooked up with the two fellas from the Jazz Is Dead label and I just find it an interesting pairing.

Well that’s the biggest trick that’s been played on me in my life. They said, “Look, man, we’ve got some hip-hop tracks and we want to dub you on a couple of them. Gary Bartz is going to do some and Roy Ayers is going to do some.” I said, “Okay, how much you going to pay me?” So we agreed on a price but they didn’t say the name on the label is going to be Jazz Is Dead, and be promoting a concept named Jazz Is Dead. They didn’t’ say nothing about that. I didn’t know nothing about that until it came out. And when I…

“tricked me” I don’t mean a dirty stab in the back trick you know, they just didn’t say nothing about it you know. And that didn’t rattle me too much you know, but we played a gig and we’d go in the auditorium and all these Jazz Is Dead posters was all over the walls and it was kind of discouraging you know, but they’re intelligent young men, they’re clean cut and I give them a break. But I tell any young people, older people too, if you’re going to tear something down and destroy it, make sure you’ve got…
